strategy.summary: GET /products filters the in-memory catalogue by a case-insensitive name substring `q`, pages with `limit` (default 20, capped at MAX_LIMIT) and `offset`, and returns { total, items }. Tests start the real app in-process (as test/products.test.js does) and prove filtering, paging, total, the cap and the 400 refusals.
inScope: GET /products query filtering, paging, total, limit cap, validation of limit/offset
outOfScope: GET /products/:id and POST /orders (not part of this ticket)
assumptions: The code's cap MAX_LIMIT = 50 is correct, not the README's 100 (asked as Q1); tests import MAX_LIMIT and DEFAULT_LIMIT from src/app.js.

The app runs for real in-process on an OS-chosen port; nothing is faked. Expected matches are computed from the exported PRODUCTS catalogue (fixed data), not hard-coded beyond what the catalogue defines.
Results are in catalogue (id) order, as the README says, so pages can be compared to slices of the expected matches.
openQuestions: README says limit is capped at 100; code caps at 50. Which is right?

risks.description: Paging returns overlapping/missing items or a total that counts only the page
risks.mitigation: TC3/TC4 compare consecutive pages and total to the full filtered list

risks.description: Unbounded limit lets clients pull the whole catalogue
risks.mitigation: TC5 asserts exactly MAX_LIMIT items for a larger limit

risks.description: Malformed paging values silently accepted (NaN slice returns empty/everything)
risks.mitigation: TC6-TC8 assert 400 for decimals, negatives, non-numbers and limit 0

acceptanceCriteria.text: `q` returns products whose name contains it case-insensitively; without `q` every product is listed.
`limit` and `offset` page the results, the response's `total` is the number of all matches, and limits above the maximum are capped.
A non-whole-number `limit` or `offset`, or a `limit` below 1, gets 400.

review.standard: titles identify the case and input; failures are diagnosable
review.summary: The six it.each rows all share one literal title with no $name/$value interpolation, so a failing row's report doesn't say which parameter or value was refused wrongly.
review.failureScenario: If the app started accepting offset=-1 (e.g. the regex changed to allow a sign), vitest would report 'refuses a limit or offset that is not a whole number with 400' failed, the same as five other tests, so you couldn't tell which input regressed without rerunning. Something like '... with 400 ($name=$value)' would fix it and keep the accepted case title as the prefix.

refusals.reason: `lint` isn't a package script in the root package.

questions.question: The README says `limit` is capped at 100, but src/app.js caps it at MAX_LIMIT = 50. Which cap is correct for GET /products?
questions.assumption: The code is right (cap = 50). Tests import MAX_LIMIT from src/app.js and assert that a limit above the cap returns exactly MAX_LIMIT items. The README mismatch goes in as a follow-up.
questions.answer: The cap is 50, as the code does. The README is out of date; leave it as it is and test against 50.
